Change c0389. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. III; 1831 Ch. XX.

Context before (unchanged): As I was occupied in fixing the boat and arranging the sails, several people crowded towards the spot.

1818 text: They seemed very much surprised at my appearance; but, instead of offering me any assistance, whispered together with gestures that at any other time might have produced in me a slight sensation of alarm.

1831 text: They seemed much surprised at my appearance; but, instead of offering me any assistance, whispered together with gestures that at any other time might have produced in me a slight sensation of alarm.

Diff: They seemed [-very-] much surprised at my appearance; but, instead of offering me any assistance, whispered together with gestures that at any other time might have produced in me a slight sensation of alarm.

Context after (unchanged): As it was, I merely remarked that they spoke English; and I therefore addressed them in that language: "My good friends," said I, "will you be so kind as to tell me the name of this town, and inform me where I am?"

result.rationale: Removal of the intensifier "very" in "very much surprised" simply trims emphasis without replacing it with other material or changing events or character.
